result.rationale: In EventManager.ts the diff replaces `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` with `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null/undefined the destructure yields undefined, so accessing `.integration` throws a TypeError, whereas the old code safely fell back to the daily video location. This is a verifiable crash path for bookings with MeetLocationType and no destination calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the diff introduces `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then immediately reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining: `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]`, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and this throws a TypeError. The diff elsewhere shows `destinationCalendar` can indeed be `null` (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts` sets it to `null` when neither eventType nor organizer has one) or `[]` (multiple handlers build `destinationCalendar: []`), so this crash is verifiable from the changes.
